title: Quick Ache Composition Analysis
learningGoal: Calculate composition and recovery, evaluate consumer hypotheses, and defend the separation with report and particulate-level evidence.

actions.label: Confirm the component-percent formula

parameters.prompt: The source sentence describes dividing the sum of all recovered masses by the starting mass, which is total percent recovery, while the task asks for the percent of each component. Record which convention the instructor confirmed before any figure is submitted.
parameters.sourceAmbiguity: finding 3.7: the manual's wording describes total percent recovery, not per-component composition
parameters.note: Confirmed percent-composition convention recorded, together with the source wording it resolves.

actions.label: Calculate recovered sucrose percent by mass

parameters.formula: component dry mass / starting sample mass x 100
parameters.evidenceProvenance: recorded dry recovered mass divided by the recorded starting mass
parameters.identityLimit: This percentage describes the water-soluble fraction. Calling it sucrose is a separate claim that needs the pure-component property evidence behind it.

actions.label: Evaluate label accuracy and Team A or Team B

parameters.prompt: Compare binder with 12-18% and acetaminophen with 82-88%. Treat 15% binder and 85% acetaminophen as the label reference. Aspirin evidence supports Team B; absence of recovered aspirin is not overclaimed without method limitations.
parameters.identityLimit: The comparison is between the label's claim and the fractions actually recovered. A fraction is not the named ingredient until independent evidence says so.
parameters.note: Recovered fractions compared against the label's stated 15 % binder and 85 % acetaminophen and the accepted 12-18 % and 82-88 % ranges.
